---
title: "Example: Kaplan-Meier VPC for a time-to-event model"
description-meta: "Check a FeRx time-to-event model with a Kaplan-Meier visual predictive check: ferx_vpc_tte(), censoring like the data, stratification by covariate or dose, and competing risks."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

`ferx_vpc_tte()` is the visual predictive check for a single-event
time-to-event (TTE) endpoint. It simulates the observed design `n_sim` times,
censors each replicate like the data, and returns the observed Kaplan-Meier
curve beside the pointwise band of the replicate curves. The curve and the
band are computed in the engine; the function never refits.

::: {.callout-tip}
For the full walkthrough (dropouts, stratification, competing risks), see the
[Kaplan-Meier VPC section](https://ferx-nlme.org/ferx-book/chapters/22-time-to-event.html#sec-tte-vpc)
of Chapter 22 (Time-to-event models) in the FeRx book. All arguments are in the
[`ferx_vpc_tte()` reference](../reference/ferx_vpc_tte.qmd).
:::

## Model and data

`tte_exponential` has a constant hazard with between-subject variability, one
record per subject: `DV = 1` for an event, `DV = 0` for censoring at the end of
follow-up (30 h).

```{r model}
library(ferx)
ex <- ferx_example("tte_exponential")
ferx_model_get_section(ex$model, "event_model")
dat <- read.csv(ex$data, na.strings = ".")
table(DV = dat$DV)
```

## Fit and check

```{r fit}
fit <- ferx_fit(ex$model, ex$data, verbose = FALSE)
vpc <- ferx_vpc_tte(ex$model, ex$data, n_sim = 200, seed = 1, fit = fit)
vpc
```

The warning is the simulator's diagnostic that this example computes `LAMBDA`
in `[individual_parameters]` without using it; the `[event_model]` writes the
hazard out itself.

`vpc$observed` is the observed Kaplan-Meier curve (it matches
`survival::survfit()` row for row); `vpc$band` holds the replicate band at each
grid time: `lo`, `med` and `hi` at `probs` (5%, 50%, 95% by default) and
`n_used`, the replicates still under follow-up there.

```{r band}
head(vpc$band)
```

`plot()` uses the vpc package's `plot_vpc()` when it is installed and base
graphics otherwise; `engine = "base"` forces base graphics.

```{r plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
plot(vpc, engine = "base")
```

## Censoring

With the default `censoring = "observed"`, a subject censored in the data keeps
its censoring time in every replicate, and a subject with an event draws a
later censoring time from the censorings in the data, so the band is
comparable with the observed curve. `censoring = "horizon"` censors replicates
at the horizon only, which gives too narrow a band when subjects drop out
early. In `tte_exponential` all censoring is at the horizon, so here the two
are the same:

```{r censoring}
vpc_horizon <- ferx_vpc_tte(ex$model, ex$data, n_sim = 200, seed = 1, fit = fit,
                            censoring = "horizon")
all.equal(vpc$band, vpc_horizon$band)
```

## Stratification

`strata` names a covariate (at most 10 distinct values); `by_dose = TRUE`
groups subjects by their first dose instead. `ferx_vpc_tte()` also accepts a
data frame:

```{r strata, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
dat$ARM <- ifelse(dat$ID %% 2 == 0, 1, 2)
vpc_arm <- ferx_vpc_tte(ex$model, dat, n_sim = 200, seed = 1, fit = fit, strata = "ARM")
vpc_arm$strata
plot(vpc_arm, engine = "base")
```

## Competing risks

A model with several TTE endpoints needs `cmt`; without it the call is refused
with a `ferx_engine_error` whose code is `E_VPC_TTE_INPUT`. With `cmt`, the
curve is that cause's survival with the other causes as censoring:

```{r competing}
cr <- ferx_example("tte_competing_risks")
refusal <- tryCatch(ferx_vpc_tte(cr$model, cr$data, n_sim = 50),
                    ferx_engine_error = function(e) e)
refusal$code
ferx_vpc_tte(cr$model, cr$data, n_sim = 200, seed = 1, cmt = 2)
```

The same code refuses repeated events, delayed entry (`TENTRY`), interval
censoring and more than one record per subject on the endpoint.
